title: 10/17 shoot: reaction clips
intro: Every clip you react to, in teleprompter order: my pick, then one or two alternates.
decided: Every pick is 10 to 30 seconds (about 15 for the shorts) and starts and ends on a full sentence. I chose from the captions, not by watching, so the editor may trim a second at either end.

Clavicular: the clip already in each script stays as my pick. Nine of them cut off a word by a second or two, so I moved those edges: Looks, 70%, Tan, Sunscreen, Skin, Eyebrows, Retatrutide, Hammer and the first Face clip.
Oprah: my pick starts 32 seconds before the part the script pointed to, because that is where she says she went off it for a year and gained the weight back.
Bryan Johnson's cold room: my pick is where he cools his bed to 71 degrees and says to change your thermostat. In the part the script pointed to he only says "not too hot, not too cold".
No alternate exists for three: Retatrutide, Eyebrows and the first Face clip. He says each of those once in the whole interview.
The 70% short: the alternates do not have the 70% number. He says it once.
Hair: the alternate where he names the drugs is 22 seconds, 13 longer than my pick, so the study paragraph would have to come out of that short.
Elon Musk's posts, the Tracy Morgan quote and the cortisol TikTok have nothing to pick.
When you reply, I put the exact times into the shoot doc and the reaction clips list.
check_title: Script lines the clips do not back up (your call: change the line, change the clip, or leave it)
check: Sharon Osbourne: the script says 42 pounds in about four months. The E! clip says 42 pounds in a year.
Meghan Trainor: the two quotes in the script ("we don't lose muscle..." and "We stay in the gym") are not in this ET video. It only reads out her post saying she used Mounjaro.

Charles Barkley: the script says he gained a lot of it back. In this video he says the shortage came and he has been off it almost a year, and that he had lost 50 pounds. He does not say he regained it.
Oprah: the script says 20 pounds and "a lifetime thing". In this video she says she gained 15 pounds, and "a lifetime thing" is not said.
Bryan Johnson's son's blood: the script says he reported no benefits and stopped. In this part he says it "didn't really work" on him. He does not say he stopped.

The doctor short: the script says he is dead wrong. In the clip he says losing weight quickly by any method costs muscle, and a minute later that protein and strength training prevent it, which is the script's own point.
